name: LLM.int8() / bitsandbytes int8 (vector-wise with 16-bit outliers)
bits: w8a16 (mixed-precision decomposition: >99.9% of values multiplied in 8-bit, outlier dims in fp16)
activation_scheme: vector-wise (per inner-product / per-row) quantization constants for activations; outlier feature dimensions routed to a separate fp16 matmul
kernels: LLM.int8() vector-wise matmul + mixed-precision decomposition kernel
quality_delta: From the paper: a 175B-parameter 16/32-bit checkpoint can be loaded, converted to int8 and used with no performance degradation, with more than 99.9% of values multiplied in 8-bit (quant-llmint8-paper). No numeric benchmark delta is tabulated in the abstract, so none recorded.
notes: The important structural point: LLM.int8() is NOT W8A8. It is vector-wise 8-bit weights AND 8-bit activations, but the systematic outlier channels are split out into a second fp16 matrix multiply, so there is no true int8 x int8 tensor-core op running for the whole layer. That decomposition is what makes it work at all; it also makes it slow - it was a memory-saving technique, not a speed technique. Contrast with SmoothQuant, which genuinely reaches hardware W8A8 by moving difficulty into the weights upfront. Group size null: constants are per vector, not per fixed-size weight group.
